long_biography.plain_text:
Paul Harding Davis established Aerial Business Communications in Portsmouth in 1986 and spent three decades shaping the company. Starting as a regional telecom dealer, Aerial grew by serving small and mid-sized enterprises and became active in a consolidating market. Davis combined majority ownership with day-to-day leadership, using acquisitions to broaden the company while retaining its base in southern England.

A 2018 management buyout brought Aerial Telephones into sister company Aerial Direct and allowed Davis, by then a non-operational majority shareholder, to exit. His business focus moved to Clarendon Holdings Group, which he controls, and a group of property companies. These include a property-trading vehicle and a building-project developer, marking a shift from communications operations to real estate and investment holding.

uncertainties.detail: Identity is resolved at 99 without relying on private-vessel evidence. Exact name plus British nationality, United Kingdom residence and April 1961 birth metadata match one Companies House officer record spanning the Aerial and Clarendon companies. The Australian financial-services executive Paul Harding-Davis has a hyphenated public name, Australian career and residence and is explicitly excluded.

Companies House styles the name as DAVIS, Paul Harding, establishing Harding as a middle name. The source record already stores the nonblank last-name value as Harding Davis; proposing Harding into the blank middle-name field could duplicate it in downstream display logic, so no name-field change is proposed.

April 1961 is already present in the source record and independently matches Companies House. No reliable reviewed source establishes the exact birth day or birthplace, so both missing fields remain blank.

The 1986 founder statement survives in archived Aerial company copy reproduced by a company-data service; the current Aerial site independently traces the operating lineage to 1986, while Companies House, O2 and trade reporting confirm Davis's majority ownership and managing-director role. The combination supports Founder at very high confidence.

Aerial was founder-built and no inherited core business is documented, supporting Self-made. Public sources do not describe Davis's family resources, education, prior employment or startup financing, so neither independent-start nor advantaged-start is assigned.

The Clarendon registry chain establishes majority control and property-related business purposes, but abbreviated accounts and public filings do not rank the property companies against cash, securities or proceeds from the Aerial exit. Real Estate describes the largest identifiable current operating interest, not a complete personal balance sheet.

No exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, personal website or TikTok account cleared verification. Search results prominently return the unrelated Australian Paul Harding-Davis LinkedIn profile, which is not proposed. The current Aerial website is a company account and is used only as a source, not as a personal social.

Mobile telecommunications is the minimum useful active tag because it captures Davis's defining founder-controlled Aerial platform and O2 reseller role. Fixed-line telecommunications was an important extension but is omitted to avoid a closely overlapping second tag; Property developer was considered but omitted because registry activity alone does not establish it as a sufficiently recognised public occupation.
No dedicated Forbes person profile was found. Searches using the exact name and Aerial and Clarendon company names did not produce a defensible Forbes social or reliable public net-worth figure.

Both biographies exclude every private-vessel name, ownership fact, registration, specification, holding structure and value. They also omit private addresses, unverified sale proceeds, personal-property values and balance-sheet extrapolations.
